surfaced_pitfalls.finding: The 09aea8b3 worker wrote its conflict resolution into the PARENT checkout's crates/jit/src/profile/package.rs instead of its worktree. Its shell commands were correctly prefixed with an absolute cd, but its file-editing tool resolves relative paths against the parent checkout, which the shell prefix does not affect.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Detected by check-leak-into-main.sh, reverted with git restore, worker instructed to use the absolute worktree path in every file-editing call. Dispatch briefs should state the path rule for FILE-EDITING TOOLS specifically, not only for shell commands — the current wording only covers the shell.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: scripts/verify-commit-builds.sh reports a cold `cargo build --workspace` of a fresh git-archive extraction as passing in 24-30 seconds, with no sccache, no RUSTC_WRAPPER, no VERIFY_COMMIT_TARGET_DIR, and an empty cache directory. A genuine cold build of this workspace's 260 dependencies cannot complete in that time, so the merge-integrity guard may be reporting a vacuous PASS.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Not investigated further inside this container: main's compile integrity is independently evidenced by cargo-ci, which runs `cargo test --workspace` per issue and demonstrably fails on real defects (it caught the 510297e4 regression). Worth a standalone issue at epic close — a guard that cannot fail is worse than no guard, because the protocol relies on it.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: cargo-ci is not deterministic under host load. crates/server/tests/server_integration/graceful_shutdown_tests.rs::test_jit_server_shutdown_force_closes_a_stalled_connection_and_exits_zero failed the gate for 3e340587 with 'the stalled connection was dropped before the drain deadline' at load average 6-10 (a worker build running beside the gate). It passes 5/5 in isolation on the same commit. The assertion is that a stalled connection SURVIVES to a drain deadline, which is precisely what CPU contention breaks.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Not attributed to any wave-0 diff. Operationally: do not run worker builds concurrently with the gate pipeline for the rest of this container, and re-evaluate the affected gate on a quiet host rather than accepting or bypassing the failure. Worth a standalone issue at epic close — a timing-sensitive test inside the authoritative whole-workspace gate makes every issue's verdict load-dependent. Related to the known env-sensitivity of the commands::gate* lib tests.
surfaced_pitfalls.correction: Superseded: the failure is NOT load-induced flakiness. The test spends up to three consecutive 2s wait_for_close budgets after SIGTERM before asserting the stalled connection is still open, while GRACEFUL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT is 5s — so once those waits exceed 5s a CORRECT server has already force-closed the survivor and the assertion fails on conforming behaviour. It failed 2/2 whole-workspace runs including one on an idle host, and passes 10/10 in isolation. Fixed lead-direct at owner direction. The earlier 'do not run worker builds beside the gate' advice still stands on its own merits but was not the cause here.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: 0439da41's REQ-05 assertion `assert!(data.icons.is_empty())` in crates/server/src/routes.rs passed vacuously: the server test fixture declared no type hierarchy, so there were no types to resolve icons for and the endpoint's icon behaviour was never observed. a30d704d's fixture change (declaring a taxonomy, required once the compiled defaults are gone) exposed it as a cargo-ci failure on merged main.
